use.consumer: an answer field and root-candidate ranking; the oracle grades
use.route: tuned Kev -> weak model (class M) -> Sonnet (class L) -> terminal route; every step journaled (§1.0)

wordings.Q0: Which class of fault do these log lines from this service show?

wordings.Q2: From this service's own log lines, what went wrong inside it?
wordings.Q3: Classify the failure this service reports about itself.

options.connection_pool_exhaustion: the service's own client connection pool to its datastore is saturated or leaking, so its requests queue and time out while the datastore itself stays healthy (the root is the service that owns the pool, not the datastore)
options.certificate_expiry: a TLS certificate served by the service passed the end of its validity period, so clients refuse to connect to it (the root is the service whose certificate expired, not the clients that reject it)
options.bad_config_deploy: a new release or configuration rollout of the service (its version string changes) broke its behaviour
options.disk_full: the service's own storage volume ran out of free space, so its writes fail
options.dns_resolution_failure: the service can no longer resolve the hostnames of the things it calls, although those targets are healthy (the root is the service whose lookups fail)
options.memory_leak_oom: memory in the service grows without bound until the process is killed for exceeding its memory limit, and the cycle repeats after restarts
options.clock_skew: the service's system clock drifted away from real time, breaking its time-sensitive checks such as token validity windows (the root is the service whose clock is wrong)
options.upstream_rate_limiting: an external third-party provider that the service depends on started throttling its calls (the root is the internal service that calls the provider)
options.poisoned_cache: the service's cache was filled with corrupt or invalid entries that it keeps serving to its callers
